title: Properties of acids and bases

draft.title: Properties of acids and bases
card: Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus red. They react with many metals to give hydrogen gas, and with carbonates to give carbon dioxide.
Bases feel slippery and turn red litmus blue. Soap and many cleaning products contain bases.
An indicator is a substance that changes colour depending on the pH of the solution it is in. Litmus is one indicator.
Tasting and touching chemicals is not safe in a lab. Use indicators and reactions to test a solution instead.
draft.remember: Acids and bases can be told apart by how they react and by indicator colours.

a.q: A student adds a solution to blue litmus paper and the paper turns red. What does this show about the solution?
a.why: Blue litmus turns red in an acid. A base would turn red litmus blue, so it would leave blue litmus unchanged.
a.clue: Think about which type of solution turns blue litmus red.

b.q: Sam drops a piece of magnesium ribbon into a clear solution and sees bubbles. The gas is collected. Which result fits an acid reacting with a metal?
opts: No gas forms but the solution turns red
b.why: Acids react with many metals to give hydrogen gas, so bubbles from a metal fit an acid. Carbon dioxide is the gas given off when an acid reacts with a carbonate, not a metal.
b.clue: Which gas does an acid give off with a metal, not a carbonate?
